item.title: Sefa-utaki Sacred Site — Guide
item.description: Sefa-utaki, in Nanjo on the southeast of Okinawa’s main island, is the most sacred site of the indigenous Ryukyu religion and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of the Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu). Rather than a built temple, it is a sacred natural space set within lush subtropical forest — a series of worship areas among huge rock formations, where Ryukyuan kings once held ceremonies and the kingdom’s highest priestess presided over rituals.
